text:
Leo Carlsson has 28 points in 22 games, and 19 of them have come on the power play. That's the headline and the caveat at once: Anaheim has given the 21-year-old the keys, and his ice time is up more than two minutes a night over his last 10 games.

At five on five it's quieter. The Ducks have taken about 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, a little better than without him but not a line tilting the ice. He has just 6 goals on 5.5 expected and 38 shots, so the scoring is honest, just light on volume. Most of the noise around this team is about teammate Cutter Gauthier, and the setup work that feeds those goals is a big part of Carlsson's value.

The tools back it up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries last season and setting up 10.0 shots per 60, 94th percentile among forwards. Evolving-Hockey had him better than his results, 2.4 expected wins against 1.1 actual. Watch the even-strength assists; that's where a second-overall pick turns into a true number one center.
headline: Carlsson's points run through the power play
